claim: Primary hippocampal neurons were grown in a 'light' medium that contained all natural amino acids for 18–19 days in vitro (DIV).
source: Primary hippocampal neurons were grown in a 'light' medium that contained all natural amino acids. After 18–19 days in vitro (DIV), the medium was exchanged to a 'heavy' medium that contained heavy isotopically labeled arginine and lysine instead of the 'light' isotopologues.
evidence: This is a direct methodological statement describing the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: Upon medium change to heavy SILAC medium, nascent proteins mainly incorporated 'heavy' arginine and lysine so that newly synthesized proteins became 'heavy' labeled, whereas pre-existing proteins were 'light' labeled.
source: Upon the medium change, nascent proteins mainly incorporated 'heavy' arginine and lysine so that newly synthesized proteins became 'heavy' labeled, whereas pre-existing proteins were 'light' labeled.
evidence: This describes the fundamental principle of the dynamic SILAC labeling technique used in the study.

claim: Neurons were treated with bicuculline (BIC) to increase global network activity and induce homeostatic down-scaling.
source: Neurons were either treated with the GABAA-receptor antagonist bicuculline (BIC), to increase global network activity and induce homeostatic down-scaling, or with the sodium channel blocker tetrodotoxin (TTX), to decrease neuronal network activity and induce homeostatic up-scaling (Turrigiano et al., 1998) or not treated (Ctrl).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental treatments used, with citation to prior work establishing this approach.

claim: Neurons were treated with tetrodotoxin (TTX) to decrease neuronal network activity and induce homeostatic up-scaling.
source: Neurons were either treated with the GABAA-receptor antagonist bicuculline (BIC), to increase global network activity and induce homeostatic down-scaling, or with the sodium channel blocker tetrodotoxin (TTX), to decrease neuronal network activity and induce homeostatic up-scaling (Turrigiano et al., 1998) or not treated (Ctrl).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental treatments used, with citation to prior work establishing this approach.

claim: Cells were treated and heavy labeled for 1, 3 or 7 days.
source: The cells were treated and heavy labeled for 1, 3 or 7 days.
evidence: This describes the time points used in the experimental design.

claim: Heavy peptides could be robustly detected and quantified even after 1 day of heavy SILAC pulse.
source: As demonstrated previously (Dörrbaum et al., 2018), heavy peptides could be robustly detected and quantified even after 1 day of heavy SILAC pulse (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to a previous study and to supplementary figure data in the current manuscript.

claim: BIC-treated neurons exhibited significantly decreased mEPSC amplitudes compared to control neurons after 7 days of treatment.
source: BIC-treated neurons exhibited significantly decreased mEPSCs amplitudes compared to control neurons (unpaired t-test, p=0.009).
evidence: This is a statistical result from electrophysiological measurements comparing treated and control neurons.

claim: TTX-treated neurons exhibited significantly increased mEPSC amplitudes compared to control neurons after 7 days of treatment.
source: TTX-treated neurons exhibited significantly increased mEPSCs amplitudes compared to control neurons (unpaired t-test, p=0.005).
evidence: This is a statistical result from electrophysiological measurements comparing treated and control neurons.

claim: The treatments induced homeostatic scaling over the entire duration of the experiment (7 days).
source: Consistently, decreased or increased mEPSC amplitudes were also observed after 7 days of BIC treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B) or TTX treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D), respectively, demonstrating that the treatments induced homeostatic scaling over the entire duration of the experiment.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the electrophysiological data showing sustained effects of the treatments.

claim: Under basal neuronal activity (Ctrl), a median protein half-life of 5.3 days was observed.
source: Under basal neuronal activity (Ctrl), a median protein half-life of 5.3 days was observed, which is consistent with previous studies from our lab (median half-life of 5.4 days) (Dörrbaum et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the protein turnover analysis, with comparison to previous work.

claim: Upon TTX-induced homeostatic up-scaling, the protein half-life distribution was significantly shifted towards longer half-lives (median half-life 5.7 days).
source: Upon TTX-induced homeostatic up-scaling, the protein half-life distribution was significantly shifted towards longer half-lives (median half-life 5.7 days; Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the protein turnover analysis comparing TTX treatment to control.

claim: Upon BIC-induced down-scaling, an even stronger shift towards longer protein half-lives was observed (median half-life 6.1 days).
source: An even stronger shift towards longer protein half-lives was observed upon BIC-induced down-scaling (median half-life 6.1 days; Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001), demonstrating that the neuronal proteome dynamics are affected by homeostatic scaling.
evidence: This is a statistical result from the protein turnover analysis comparing BIC treatment to control.

claim: The neuronal proteome dynamics are affected by homeostatic scaling.
source: An even stronger shift towards longer protein half-lives was observed upon BIC-induced down-scaling (median half-life 6.1 days; Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001), demonstrating that the neuronal proteome dynamics are affected by homeostatic scaling.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observed changes in protein half-life distributions during homeostatic scaling.

claim: In total, 7150 proteins were identified throughout all experimental conditions.
source: In total, we identified 7150 proteins throughout all experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: After stringent filtering for dataset completeness, 3596 proteins were quantified for the down-scaling versus control comparison.
source: After stringent filtering for dataset completeness, 3596 proteins were quantified for the down-scaling versus control comparison and 3609 proteins were quantified for the up-scaling versus control comparison (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result describing the number of proteins analyzed after quality filtering.

claim: 3609 proteins were quantified for the up-scaling versus control comparison.
source: After stringent filtering for dataset completeness, 3596 proteins were quantified for the down-scaling versus control comparison and 3609 proteins were quantified for the up-scaling versus control comparison (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result describing the number of proteins analyzed after quality filtering.

claim: Upon induction of homeostatic down-scaling (BIC treatment), 43% of the quantified proteome showed changes in protein synthesis and/or degradation.
source: Upon induction of homeostatic down-scaling (BIC treatment), a large fraction of the quantified proteome (43%), showed changes in protein synthesis and/or degradation (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of protein synthesis and degradation during BIC treatment.

claim: During BIC-induced down-scaling, the regulation was biased toward decreased protein synthesis and/or degradation.
source: Generally speaking, the regulation was biased toward decreased protein synthesis and/or degradation.
evidence: This is a summary observation from the data on protein regulation during down-scaling.

claim: During BIC-induced down-scaling, 703 proteins exhibited decreased synthesis rates.
source: Of the regulated proteins, the largest group were proteins that exhibited decreased synthesis rates (703 proteins), followed by those exhibiting decreased degradation rates (496 proteins) and those exhibiting decreased protein turnover rates (less synthesis together with less degradation; 292 proteins).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of protein regulation during BIC treatment.

claim: During BIC-induced down-scaling, 496 proteins exhibited decreased degradation rates.
source: Of the regulated proteins, the largest group were proteins that exhibited decreased synthesis rates (703 proteins), followed by those exhibiting decreased degradation rates (496 proteins) and those exhibiting decreased protein turnover rates (less synthesis together with less degradation; 292 proteins).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of protein regulation during BIC treatment.

claim: During BIC-induced down-scaling, 292 proteins exhibited decreased protein turnover rates (less synthesis together with less degradation).
source: Of the regulated proteins, the largest group were proteins that exhibited decreased synthesis rates (703 proteins), followed by those exhibiting decreased degradation rates (496 proteins) and those exhibiting decreased protein turnover rates (less synthesis together with less degradation; 292 proteins).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of protein regulation during BIC treatment.

claim: During BIC-induced down-scaling, only 18 proteins showed increased synthesis rates.
source: By contrast, only a few proteins showed increased synthesis rates (18 proteins), increased synthesis rates together with decreased degradation rates (nine proteins), increased degradation rates (11 proteins) or increased degradation rates together with reduced synthesis rates (13 proteins; Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of protein regulation during BIC treatment.

claim: Reduced protein degradation and reduced protein synthesis are the preferred cellular mechanisms to achieve changes in protein abundance during homeostatic down-scaling.
source: These results suggest that reduced protein degradation and reduced protein synthesis are the preferred cellular mechanisms to achieve changes in protein abundance during homeostatic down-scaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data showing that most regulated proteins exhibited decreased synthesis or degradation.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 31% of the quantified proteins showed a change in synthesis and/or degradation.
source: During up-scaling, 31% of the quantified proteins showed a change in synthesis and/or degradation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of protein synthesis and degradation during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 503 proteins were regulated by a decrease in synthesis.
source: Similar to the results for homeostatic down-scaling, following up-scaling, the largest groups of proteins were regulated by a decrease in synthesis (503 proteins), with the second-largest group being regulated by a decrease in degradation (332 proteins; Figure 2E–F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of protein regulation during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 332 proteins were regulated by a decrease in degradation.
source: Similar to the results for homeostatic down-scaling, following up-scaling, the largest groups of proteins were regulated by a decrease in synthesis (503 proteins), with the second-largest group being regulated by a decrease in degradation (332 proteins; Figure 2E–F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of protein regulation during TTX treatment.

claim: Reduced protein degradation might be generally preferred over increased protein synthesis to achieve long-term proteomic up-regulation.
source: This suggests that reduced protein degradation might be generally preferred over increased protein synthesis to achieve long-term proteomic up-regulation, and that reduced protein synthesis might be generally preferred over increased protein degradation to achieve long-term proteomic down-regulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data showing similar patterns of regulation during both up- and down-scaling.

claim: Reduced protein synthesis might be generally preferred over increased protein degradation to achieve long-term proteomic down-regulation.
source: This suggests that reduced protein degradation might be generally preferred over increased protein synthesis to achieve long-term proteomic up-regulation, and that reduced protein synthesis might be generally preferred over increased protein degradation to achieve long-term proteomic down-regulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data showing similar patterns of regulation during both up- and down-scaling.

claim: Protein synthesis was significantly reduced during BIC-induced down-scaling after 24 hr of treatment.
source: Western blot analysis revealed that protein synthesis was significantly reduced during BIC-induced down-scaling (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a result from western blot analysis of AHA-labeled nascent proteins.

claim: Protein synthesis was slightly decreased during TTX-induced up-scaling after 24 hr of treatment, although the difference did not reach statistical significance.
source: Protein synthesis was also slightly decreased during TTX-induced up-scaling, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a result from western blot analysis of AHA-labeled nascent proteins.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α at Ser51 was significantly increased after 24 hr of treatment with BIC.
source: Phosphorylation of eIF2α at Ser51 was significantly increased after 24 hr of treatment with BIC (unpaired t-test, p-value<0.001) and TTX (unpaired t-test, p-value<0.01).
evidence: This is a statistical result from western blot analysis of phosphorylated eIF2α.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α at Ser51 was significantly increased after 24 hr of treatment with TTX.
source: Phosphorylation of eIF2α at Ser51 was significantly increased after 24 hr of treatment with BIC (unpaired t-test, p-value<0.001) and TTX (unpaired t-test, p-value<0.01).
evidence: This is a statistical result from western blot analysis of phosphorylated eIF2α.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α at Ser51 inhibits translation.
source: Translation initiation is catalyzed by multiple initiation factors and is a major target of translational control. For example, phosphorylation of the eukaryotic initiation factor two alpha (eIF2α) at Ser51 inhibits translation (Dever, 2002; Hinnebusch, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: The changes in Ser51 phosphorylation correlate well with the decrease in protein synthesis observed by SILAC-MS and western blot analysis.
source: The changes in Ser51 phosphorylation correlate well with the decrease in protein synthesis observed by SILAC-MS and western blot analysis.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the eIF2α phosphorylation data with the protein synthesis measurements.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α leads to a paradoxical increase in the translation of mRNAs that contain upstream open reading frames (uORFs) in their 5′-UTRs.
source: Despite a general inhibition of translation initiation, phosphorylation of eIF2α also leads to a paradoxical increase in the translation of mRNAs that contain upstream open reading frames (uORFs) in their 5′-UTRs (Dever, 2002; Hinnebusch, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: uORF-containing genes are significantly over-represented in the group of proteins that showed increased synthesis during TTX treatment.
source: uORF-containing genes are significantly over-represented in the group of proteins that showed increased synthesis during TTX treatment (hypergeometric test, p<0.05) and significantly under-represented in the group of proteins that did not show increased synthesis during TTX treatment (hypergeometric test, p<0.05).
evidence: This is a statistical result from enrichment analysis of uORF-containing genes.

claim: uORF-containing genes are significantly under-represented in the group of proteins that did not show increased synthesis during TTX treatment.
source: uORF-containing genes are significantly over-represented in the group of proteins that showed increased synthesis during TTX treatment (hypergeometric test, p<0.05) and significantly under-represented in the group of proteins that did not show increased synthesis during TTX treatment (hypergeometric test, p<0.05).
evidence: This is a statistical result from enrichment analysis of uORF-containing genes.

claim: No change in proteasome activity was detected during homeostatic scaling.
source: Although decreased degradation rates were also observed for large numbers of proteins during homeostatic up- and down-scaling (Figure 2B–F), we did not detect changes in the activity of proteasomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) or differences in ongoing autophagy (Figure 3—figure supplement 3; Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a result from proteasome activity assays.

claim: No differences in ongoing autophagy were detected during homeostatic scaling.
source: Although decreased degradation rates were also observed for large numbers of proteins during homeostatic up- and down-scaling (Figure 2B–F), we did not detect changes in the activity of proteasomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) or differences in ongoing autophagy (Figure 3—figure supplement 3; Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a result from autophagy marker analysis.

claim: All neuronal preparations were visually inspected under the microscope prior to harvest and no signs of stress or apoptosis (blebbing or fragmenting in the dendrites) were observed.
source: To exclude the possibility that the observed changes in protein synthesis and degradation were a result of cellular stress, all neuronal preparations were visually inspected under the microscope prior to harvest and no signs of stress or apoptosis (blebbing or fragmenting in the dendrites) were observed.
evidence: This is a methodological control to ensure cell viability.

claim: No increase in the degradation of Caspase-3 was observed in BIC- and TTX-treated hippocampal cultures in comparison to untreated controls, indicating that the treatment did not impair cell viability.
source: No increase in the degradation of Casp-3 was observed in BIC- and TTX-treated hippocampal cultures in comparison to untreated controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), indicating that the treatment did not impair cell viability.
evidence: This is a result from analysis of the apoptotic marker Caspase-3 in the MS data.

claim: During BIC-induced down-scaling, 59% of the synaptic proteins showed a change in synthesis and/or degradation.
source: During BIC-induced down-scaling, 59% of the synaptic proteins showed a change in synthesis and/or degradation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from analysis of synaptic protein regulation.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 52% of the synaptic proteins showed a change in synthesis and/or degradation.
source: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 52% of the synaptic proteins showed a change in synthesis and/or degradation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from analysis of synaptic protein regulation.

claim: The dataset contains 301 quantified synaptic proteins during homeostatic down-scaling.
source: Our dataset contains numerous synaptic proteins and we were able to quantify the behavior of 301 and 302 synaptic proteins during homeostatic down-scaling (Figure 4) and up-scaling (Figure 5), respectively, of which large fractions exhibited regulation.
evidence: This is a quantitative result describing the number of synaptic proteins analyzed.

claim: The dataset contains 302 quantified synaptic proteins during homeostatic up-scaling.
source: Our dataset contains numerous synaptic proteins and we were able to quantify the behavior of 301 and 302 synaptic proteins during homeostatic down-scaling (Figure 4) and up-scaling (Figure 5), respectively, of which large fractions exhibited regulation.
evidence: This is a quantitative result describing the number of synaptic proteins analyzed.

claim: Most synaptic proteins were down-regulated upon BIC treatment.
source: Consistent with the concept of synaptic down-scaling, most synaptic proteins were down-regulated upon BIC treatment.
evidence: This is a summary observation from the synaptic protein data during BIC treatment.

claim: For most down-regulated synaptic proteins during BIC treatment, the mechanism of down-regulation is a decrease in protein synthesis.
source: For most of these proteins, the mechanism of down-regulation is a decrease in protein synthesis.
evidence: This is a summary observation from the synaptic protein data during BIC treatment.

claim: The AMPAR subunits GluA1 and GluA3 showed decreased synthesis during BIC-induced down-scaling.
source: Prominent examples in this group of proteins were the AMPAR subunits GluA1 and GluA3, fitting with the observation that AMPAR surface expression is decreased during homeostatic down-scaling (Turrigiano, 2012; Turrigiano, 2008).
evidence: This is a specific result from the protein regulation analysis, with citation to prior work on AMPAR surface expression.

claim: No significant change in degradation was observed for GluA1 and GluA3 during BIC-induced down-scaling.
source: Interestingly, no significant change in degradation was observed for GluA1 and GluA3.
evidence: This is a specific result from the protein regulation analysis.

claim: Under basal neuronal activity, the half-life of GluA1 is 2.8 days.
source: Under basal neuronal activity, the half-lives of GluA1 and GluA3 are 2.8 days and 3.5 days, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the protein turnover analysis.

claim: Under basal neuronal activity, the half-life of GluA3 is 3.5 days.
source: Under basal neuronal activity, the half-lives of GluA1 and GluA3 are 2.8 days and 3.5 days, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the protein turnover analysis.

claim: Long-lasting changes of AMPAR surface expression (in the range of days) during homeostatic down-scaling are probably accomplished by continuous degradation of pre-existing copies at an unchanged degradation rate, together with a decreased supply of newly synthesized copies.
source: These results indicate that long-lasting changes of AMPAR surface expression (in the range of days) during homeostatic down-scaling are probably accomplished by continuous degradation of pre-existing copies at an unchanged degradation rate, together with a decreased supply of newly synthesized copies.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GluA1 and GluA3 regulation data.

claim: Increased protein synthesis was observed for GluA1 during TTX-induced up-scaling, but not for GluA2 and GluA3.
source: Consistent with the increased AMPAR surface expression observed during homeostatic up-scaling (Turrigiano, 2012; Turrigiano, 2008), increased protein synthesis was observed for GluA1, but not for GluA2 and GluA3.
evidence: This is a specific result from the protein regulation analysis during TTX treatment, with citation to prior work on AMPAR surface expression.

claim: An up-regulation of vGluT1 (by increased synthesis and decreased degradation) and vGluT2 (by increased synthesis) was observed during TTX-induced up-scaling.
source: Consistent with this, we observed an up-regulation of vGluT1 (by increased synthesis and decreased degradation) and vGluT2 (by increased synthesis) during TTX-induced up-scaling (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a specific result from the protein regulation analysis during TTX treatment.

claim: A decrease in the synthesis of vGluT1 was found during BIC-induced down-scaling.
source: During BIC-induced down-scaling, on the other hand, we found a decrease in the synthesis of vGluT1 (Figure 4), which could, in principle, lower vesicular neurotransmitter levels, leading to decreased mEPSC amplitudes.
evidence: This is a specific result from the protein regulation analysis during BIC treatment.

claim: Bdnf exhibited increased synthesis as well as decreased degradation during BIC-induced down-scaling.
source: The strongest up-regulation was observed for Bdnf and Pcdh8, which exhibited increased synthesis as well as decreased degradation.
evidence: This is a specific result from the protein regulation analysis during BIC treatment.

claim: Pcdh8 exhibited increased synthesis as well as decreased degradation during BIC-induced down-scaling.
source: The strongest up-regulation was observed for Bdnf and Pcdh8, which exhibited increased synthesis as well as decreased degradation.
evidence: This is a specific result from the protein regulation analysis during BIC treatment.

claim: Bdnf is released in a calcium- and activity-dependent manner and was one of the first proteins implicated in homeostatic scaling.
source: Bdnf is released in a calcium- and activity-dependent manner, and was one of the first proteins implicated in homeostatic scaling (Rutherford et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Bdnf is required for and negatively regulates homeostatic up-scaling.
source: Rutherford et al. (1998) showed that Bdnf is required for and negatively regulates homeostatic up-scaling.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Pcdh8 (also named Arcadlin) is an activity-induced protocadherin that binds to N-cadherin to promote its endocytosis and thereby weaken synaptic connections.
source: Pcdh8 (also named Arcadlin) is an activity-induced protocadherin that binds to N-cadherin to promote its endocytosis and thereby weaken synaptic connections (Arikkath and Reichardt, 2008; Yasuda et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Upon BIC-induced down-scaling, 208 proteins were significantly decreased in abundance and 185 were significantly increased in abundance.
source: Upon BIC-induced down-scaling, 208 proteins were significantly decreased in abundance and 185 were significantly increased in abundance (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the protein abundance analysis.

claim: Upon TTX-induced up-scaling, 459 proteins were significantly increased and 493 proteins were significantly decreased in abundance.
source: Upon TTX-induced up-scaling, 459 proteins were significantly increased and 493 proteins were significantly decreased in abundance (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the protein abundance analysis.

claim: The number of significantly regulated proteins was considerably lower when analyzing changes in relative protein abundance compared to changes in the nascent proteome (synthesis) and pre-existing proteome (degradation) separately.
source: Although the number of analyzed proteins was similar, the number of significantly regulated proteins was considerably lower when analyzing changes in relative protein abundance compared to changes in the nascent proteome (synthesis) and pre-existing proteome (degradation) separately.
evidence: This is an observation comparing different analysis approaches.

claim: Many proteins showed decreased synthesis as well as decreased degradation, leading to a slower protein turnover while protein abundance remains mostly unaffected.
source: There are two reasons for this discrepancy. First, many proteins showed decreased synthesis as well as decreased degradation, leading to a slower protein turnover (Figure 2B), while protein abundance remains mostly unaffected.
evidence: This is an explanation for why fewer proteins show significant abundance changes compared to synthesis/degradation changes.

claim: The independent analysis of the nascent or pre-existing proteome is more sensitive to small changes in protein synthesis or degradation, respectively, compared to the analysis of the entire proteome.
source: Second, the independent analysis of the nascent or pre-existing proteome is more sensitive to small changes in protein synthesis or degradation, respectively, compared to the analysis of the entire proteome.
evidence: This is an explanation for why fewer proteins show significant abundance changes compared to synthesis/degradation changes.

claim: Distinct sets of proteins showed significant changes in abundance exclusively upon BIC-induced down-scaling (197 proteins) or TTX-induced up-scaling (735 proteins).
source: A comparison of the regulation observed upon both treatments revealed that distinct sets of proteins showed significant changes in abundance exclusively upon BIC-induced down-scaling (197 proteins) or TTX-induced up-scaling (735 proteins; Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing protein abundance changes between treatments.

claim: At least in part, different proteins are responsible for the phenotypes of homeostatic up- and down-scaling.
source: This observation suggests that, at least in part, different proteins are responsible for the phenotypes of homeostatic up- and down-scaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data showing treatment-specific protein regulation.

claim: Significantly more proteins showed changes in abundance during both treatments (194 proteins) than expected by chance.
source: However, this comparison also revealed that significantly more proteins showed changes in abundance during both treatments (194 proteins) than expected by chance (Fisher's exact test), suggesting that partially overlapping sets of regulated proteins were responsible for up- and down-scaling.
evidence: This is a statistical result from comparing protein abundance changes between treatments.

claim: 35 proteins were up-regulated during both up-scaling and down-scaling.
source: 35 proteins (e.g. Scg2) were up-regulated during up-scaling and down-scaling, and 66 proteins (e.g. Synpo) were down-regulated during both treatments.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing protein abundance changes between treatments.

claim: 66 proteins were down-regulated during both up-scaling and down-scaling.
source: 35 proteins (e.g. Scg2) were up-regulated during up-scaling and down-scaling, and 66 proteins (e.g. Synpo) were down-regulated during both treatments.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing protein abundance changes between treatments.

claim: 53 proteins were up-regulated upon TTX-induced up-scaling and down-regulated upon BIC-induced down-scaling.
source: 53 proteins were up-regulated upon TTX-induced up-scaling and down-regulated upon BIC-induced down-scaling (e.g. Nptx1, Homer1 and Scg1) and 40 proteins were up-regulated during BIC-induced down-scaling and down-regulated during TTX-induced up-scaling (e.g. Pcdh8, Pcdh17, Vgf and several ribosomal proteins).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing protein abundance changes between treatments.

claim: 40 proteins were up-regulated during BIC-induced down-scaling and down-regulated during TTX-induced up-scaling.
source: 53 proteins were up-regulated upon TTX-induced up-scaling and down-regulated upon BIC-induced down-scaling (e.g. Nptx1, Homer1 and Scg1) and 40 proteins were up-regulated during BIC-induced down-scaling and down-regulated during TTX-induced up-scaling (e.g. Pcdh8, Pcdh17, Vgf and several ribosomal proteins).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing protein abundance changes between treatments.

claim: Proteins that show the same regulation upon both treatments might be 'general plasticity proteins' that are involved in sensing an offset from basal activity levels, regardless of the sign of that offset.
source: Proteins that show the same regulation upon both treatments might be 'general plasticity proteins' that are involved in sensing an offset from basal activity levels, regardless of the sign of that offset.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data showing proteins regulated in the same direction by both treatments.

claim: Proteins that show opposite regulation upon the opposite treatments might be 'polarity proteins' that sense the polarity of the offset or determine the polarity of the compensatory scaling.
source: By contrast, proteins that show opposite regulation upon the opposite treatments might be 'polarity proteins' that sense the polarity of the offset or determine the polarity of the compensatory scaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data showing proteins regulated in opposite directions by the two treatments.

claim: Changes in the nascent proteome mainly drive homeostatic scaling and determine the polarity of the scaling.
source: The fact that most over-represented combinations involve a change in protein synthesis for both treatments suggests that changes in the nascent proteome mainly drive homeostatic scaling and determine the polarity of the scaling, consistent with the fact that protein synthesis is required for homeostatic scaling (Schanzenbächer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on regulation patterns, with citation to prior work showing protein synthesis is required for homeostatic scaling.

claim: After 1 day of BIC treatment, more than 600 proteins exhibited a change in synthesis.
source: After 1 day of BIC treatment, more than 600 proteins exhibited a change in synthesis and, on average, protein synthesis rates were reduced by approximately 20% compared to untreated controls (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from temporal analysis of protein synthesis during BIC treatment.

claim: After 1 day of BIC treatment, on average, protein synthesis rates were reduced by approximately 20% compared to untreated controls.
source: After 1 day of BIC treatment, more than 600 proteins exhibited a change in synthesis and, on average, protein synthesis rates were reduced by approximately 20% compared to untreated controls (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from temporal analysis of protein synthesis during BIC treatment.

claim: During BIC-induced down-scaling, the average fold-change and the average regulation strength of protein synthesis decreased over time.
source: While the average fold-change (Figure 7A) and the average regulation strength (Figure 7B) of protein synthesis decreased over time, the opposite trend was observed for protein degradation.
evidence: This is a result from temporal analysis of protein synthesis and degradation during BIC treatment.

claim: During BIC-induced down-scaling, the opposite trend was observed for protein degradation compared to protein synthesis (increasing over time).
source: While the average fold-change (Figure 7A) and the average regulation strength (Figure 7B) of protein synthesis decreased over time, the opposite trend was observed for protein degradation.
evidence: This is a result from temporal analysis of protein synthesis and degradation during BIC treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, the numbers of proteins with significantly regulated synthesis rates increased over time.
source: During TTX-induced up-scaling, the numbers of proteins with significantly regulated synthesis rates increased over time (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a result from temporal analysis of protein synthesis during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, protein sub-populations with significantly regulated synthesis showed, on average, a decrease in protein synthesis with the strongest average decrease observed after 3 days of treatment.
source: These protein sub-populations showed, on average, a decrease in protein synthesis with the strongest average decrease observed after 3 days of treatment.
evidence: This is a result from temporal analysis of protein synthesis during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, the sub-populations of proteins with significantly altered degradation rates showed, on average, a decrease in degradation for all time points.
source: The sub-populations of proteins with significantly altered degradation rates showed, on average, a decrease in degradation for all time points.
evidence: This is a result from temporal analysis of protein degradation during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, both the average fold change and the average regulation strength of protein degradation increased over time.
source: Both the average fold change (Figure 7C) and the average regulation strength (Figure 7D) increased over time.
evidence: This is a result from temporal analysis of protein degradation during TTX treatment.

claim: 192 proteins belong to clusters that showed a persistent decrease in protein synthesis during BIC-induced down-scaling.
source: 192 proteins belong to clusters that showed a persistent decrease in protein synthesis (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of temporal protein profiles during BIC treatment.

claim: PSD-95 showed a persistent decrease in protein synthesis during BIC-induced down-scaling.
source: These clusters contain many synaptic proteins, such as the postsynaptic scaffold protein PSD-95 (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a specific example from the clustering analysis.

claim: 184 proteins belong to clusters that showed a transient decrease in protein synthesis after 1 day of BIC treatment ('early peak').
source: 184 proteins belong to clusters that showed a transient decrease in protein synthesis after 1 day of BIC treatment ('early peak'), such as the candidate plasticity gene 2 (Cpg2), which is involved in activity-dependent AMPAR internalization (Loebrich et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of temporal protein profiles during BIC treatment.

claim: 337 proteins showed a transient change in protein synthesis after 3 days of BIC treatment ('intermediate peak').

claim: Bdnf showed the strongest increase in synthesis after 1 day of BIC treatment and decreasing regulation strength after 3 and 7 days of treatment.
source: A representative protein of this group is Bdnf, which showed the strongest increase in synthesis after 1 day of BIC treatment and decreasing regulation strength after 3 and 7 days of treatment.

evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of temporal protein profiles during BIC treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, no clusters with persistent changes in synthesis over the entire time course or with transient changes in synthesis after 1 day of treatment were observed.

evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of temporal protein profiles during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 231 proteins were assigned to clusters that showed transient changes in synthesis after 3 days ('intermediate peak').
source: Instead, more proteins were assigned to clusters that showed transient changes in synthesis after 3 days (231 proteins; 'intermediate peak'), 3 days and 7 days (287 proteins; 'intermediate and late peak') or 7 days (294 proteins; 'late peak') of treatment.
evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of temporal protein profiles during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 287 proteins were assigned to clusters that showed transient changes in synthesis after 3 days and 7 days ('intermediate and late peak').
source: Instead, more proteins were assigned to clusters that showed transient changes in synthesis after 3 days (231 proteins; 'intermediate peak'), 3 days and 7 days (287 proteins; 'intermediate and late peak') or 7 days (294 proteins; 'late peak') of treatment.
evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of temporal protein profiles during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 294 proteins were assigned to clusters that showed transient changes in synthesis after 7 days ('late peak').

evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of temporal protein profiles during TTX treatment.

claim: During TTX-induced up-scaling, 135 proteins showed an increasing regulation strength over time.
source: In contrast to BIC-induced down-scaling, 135 proteins showed an increasing regulation strength over time, whereas only 20 proteins showed a decreasing regulation strength.
evidence: This is a result from clustering analysis of temporal protein profiles during TTX treatment.

claim: The neuronal proteome was massively remodeled during both down-scaling and up-scaling.
source: Here, we used dynamic SILAC labeling and MS to quantify changes in protein synthesis, degradation, abundance and turnover during homeostatic scaling in cultured neurons. We found that the neuronal proteome was massively remodeled during both down-scaling and up-scaling.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the overall results of the study.

claim: Synaptic proteins were especially affected by the scaling.
source: Synaptic proteins were especially affected by the scaling.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the analysis of synaptic protein regulation.

claim: More than half of the quantified synaptic proteins were regulated during homeostatic scaling.
source: More than half of the quantified synaptic proteins were regulated.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the analysis of synaptic protein regulation.

claim: Most proteins exhibited a decrease in synthesis or degradation during homeostatic scaling.
source: Most proteins exhibited a decrease in synthesis or degradation, whereas only a few proteins showed increased synthesis rates.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the overall protein regulation analysis.

claim: Only a few proteins showed increased synthesis rates during homeostatic scaling.
source: Most proteins exhibited a decrease in synthesis or degradation, whereas only a few proteins showed increased synthesis rates.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the overall protein regulation analysis.

claim: Decreased protein synthesis or degradation might be a generally preferred mechanism to accomplish long-term changes in the neuronal proteome.
source: Our data demonstrate that decreased protein degradation and decreased protein synthesis are the preferred cellular mechanisms to achieve increased or decreased protein abundance, respectively, during homeostatic scaling. This preference was observed for both homeostatic up- and down-scaling, suggesting that decreasing protein synthesis or degradation might be a generally preferred mechanism to accomplish long-term changes in the neuronal proteome.
evidence: This is an interpretation and generalization from the observed patterns of protein regulation.

claim: Reduced protein synthesis or degradation rates might be preferred over increased degradation or synthesis rates, respectively, because it is the more energy-saving way to achieve proteomic changes.
source: Reduced protein synthesis or degradation rates might be preferred over increased degradation or synthesis rates, respectively, because it is the more energy-saving way to achieve proteomic changes.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed preference for decreased synthesis/degradation.

claim: The signal processing power, and hence the cognitive capability, of the brain is limited by the availability of energy.
source: The signal processing power, and hence the cognitive capability, of the brain is limited by the availability of energy.
evidence: This is general knowledge about brain energetics.

claim: Most of the brain's energy budget is required for signaling-related processes, and reduced 'housekeeping costs' (including costs associated with protein synthesis and degradation), provide a cognitive advantage.
source: Most of the brain's energy budget is required for signaling-related processes, and reduced 'housekeeping costs' (including costs associated with protein synthesis and degradation), provide a cognitive advantage (Engl and Attwell, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α was previously identified as an underlying mechanism of long-term depression induced by metabotropic glutamate receptor activation (mGluR-LTD).
source: Phosphorylation of eIF2α was previously identified as an underlying mechanism of long-term depression induced by metabotropic glutamate receptor activation (mGluR-LTD), another protein synthesis-dependent form of synaptic plasticity (Di Prisco et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Bidirectional transcriptional regulation has been observed in previous studies after 6 hr of BIC or TTX treatment in primary cortical cultures.
source: Consistently, bidirectional transcriptional regulation has been observed in previous studies after 6 hr of BIC or TTX treatment in primary cortical cultures (Schaukowitch et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Post-transcriptional regulation by micro-RNAs, which regulate the pool of 'translatable' mRNAs, are critically involved in homeostatic up-scaling.
source: Previous studies demonstrated that post-transcriptional regulation by micro-RNAs, which regulate the pool of 'translatable' mRNAs, are critically involved in homeostatic up-scaling (Cohen et al., 2011; Fiore et al., 2014) as well as in down-scaling (Hou et al., 2015; Letellier et al., 2014; Rajman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Post-transcriptional regulation by micro-RNAs are critically involved in homeostatic down-scaling.
source: Previous studies demonstrated that post-transcriptional regulation by micro-RNAs, which regulate the pool of 'translatable' mRNAs, are critically involved in homeostatic up-scaling (Cohen et al., 2011; Fiore et al., 2014) as well as in down-scaling (Hou et al., 2015; Letellier et al., 2014; Rajman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Protein degradation is regulated at the level of ubiquitin ligation by specific E3 ligases during homeostatic scaling.
source: Despite the general decrease in protein degradation observed in our data, no change in proteasome activity or ongoing autophagy was observed, suggesting that protein degradation is regulated at the level of ubiquitin ligation by specific E3 ligases.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that degradation changes occur without changes in proteasome activity or autophagy.

claim: Extensive changes in both postsynaptic and presynaptic proteins were observed during homeostatic scaling, suggesting that both sides of the synapse are modified.
source: Of note, we observed extensive changes in both postsynaptic and presynaptic proteins, suggesting that both sides of the synapse are modified during homeostatic scaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of regulation in both pre- and postsynaptic proteins.

claim: It is generally agreed that homeostatic scaling at mammalian synapses uses postsynaptic mechanisms that evoke changes in AMPAR surface expression.
source: It is generally agreed that homeostatic scaling at mammalian synapses uses postsynaptic mechanisms that evoke changes in AMPAR surface expression.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Presynaptic mechanisms also contribute to homeostatic scaling.
source: Presynaptic mechanisms are less explored, but also contribute to homeostatic scaling (Davis and Müller, 2015; Murthy et al., 2001; Turrigiano, 2012; Vitureira et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Previous studies have described enhanced glutamate transporter (vGluT) expression in pre-synaptic terminals upon activity blockade.
source: For instance, previous studies have described enhanced glutamate transporter (vGluT) expression in pre-synaptic terminals upon activity blockade (De Gois et al., 2005; Erickson et al., 2006), which might enable the neurons to package more neurotransmitters into synaptic vesicles to enhance quantal signals.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Enhanced vGluT expression might enable the neurons to package more neurotransmitters into synaptic vesicles to enhance quantal signals.
source: For instance, previous studies have described enhanced glutamate transporter (vGluT) expression in pre-synaptic terminals upon activity blockade (De Gois et al., 2005; Erickson et al., 2006), which might enable the neurons to package more neurotransmitters into synaptic vesicles to enhance quantal signals.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional consequence of vGluT upregulation.

claim: The expression of Pcdh8 might bidirectionally regulate the strength of synaptic connections during homeostatic down-scaling (through increased synthesis and decreased degradation of Pcdh8) and homeostatic up-scaling (through decreased synthesis of Pcdh8).
source: Our data suggest that the expression of Pcdh8 might bidirectionally regulate the strength of synaptic connections during homeostatic down-scaling (through increased synthesis and decreased degradation of Pcdh8) and homeostatic up-scaling (through decreased synthesis of Pcdh8).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed regulation of Pcdh8 during homeostatic scaling.

claim: GluA2-lacking receptors have a higher Ca2+ permeability, channel conductance and open probability than GluA2-containing receptors.
source: GluA2-lacking receptors have a higher Ca2+ permeability, channel conductance and open probability than GluA2-containing receptors (Burnashev et al., 1992; Oh and Derkach, 2005; Swanson et al., 1997), and an increased contribution of GluA2-lacking AMPARs has been observed upon synaptic strengthening induced by long-term activity blockade by TTX and APV (Sutton et al., 2006; Thiagarajan et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: An increased contribution of GluA2-lacking AMPARs has been observed upon synaptic strengthening induced by long-term activity blockade by TTX and APV.
source: GluA2-lacking receptors have a higher Ca2+ permeability, channel conductance and open probability than GluA2-containing receptors (Burnashev et al., 1992; Oh and Derkach, 2005; Swanson et al., 1997), and an increased contribution of GluA2-lacking AMPARs has been observed upon synaptic strengthening induced by long-term activity blockade by TTX and APV (Sutton et al., 2006; Thiagarajan et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Nitric oxide synthase 1 (Nos1) is required for long-term potentiation.
source: Nitric oxide synthase 1 (Nos1) — a protein that is required for long-term potentiation (Haley et al., 1992; Hardingham et al., 2013; Schuman and Madison, 1991) — is another interesting candidate that is up-regulated by increased synthesis as well as by decreased degradation during TTX-induced up-scaling.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Nos1 is up-regulated by increased synthesis as well as by decreased degradation during TTX-induced up-scaling.
source: Nitric oxide synthase 1 (Nos1) — a protein that is required for long-term potentiation (Haley et al., 1992; Hardingham et al., 2013; Schuman and Madison, 1991) — is another interesting candidate that is up-regulated by increased synthesis as well as by decreased degradation during TTX-induced up-scaling.
evidence: This is a specific result from the protein regulation analysis during TTX treatment.

claim: Nos1 and NO signaling is also regulated by homeostatic up-scaling and might be a link between the presynaptic and postsynaptic mechanisms underlying homeostatic scaling.
source: Hence, our data suggest that Nos1 and NO signaling is also regulated by homeostatic up-scaling and might be a link between the presynaptic and postsynaptic mechanisms underlying homeostatic scaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of Nos1 regulation.

claim: Proteins that were only regulated at the first time point or that showed decreasing strength of regulation might play a role in the initiation of homeostatic scaling.
source: Proteins that were only regulated at the first time point or that showed decreasing strength of regulation (e.g. Bdnf during down-scaling; Figure 8B) might play a role in the initiation of homeostatic scaling, whereas proteins that were permanently regulated (such as PSD-95 during down-scaling; Figure 8B) might be involved in maintenance of the scaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of different temporal regulation patterns.

claim: Proteins that were permanently regulated might be involved in maintenance of homeostatic scaling.
source: Proteins that were only regulated at the first time point or that showed decreasing strength of regulation (e.g. Bdnf during down-scaling; Figure 8B) might play a role in the initiation of homeostatic scaling, whereas proteins that were permanently regulated (such as PSD-95 during down-scaling; Figure 8B) might be involved in maintenance of the scaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of different temporal regulation patterns.

claim: The use of the 'semi-heavy' internal standard enabled correction for the experimental and technical variation introduced during sample preparation and LC-MS acquisition.
source: The use of the 'semi-heavy' internal standard enabled us to correct for the experimental and technical variation introduced during sample preparation and LC-MS acquisition.
evidence: This describes a methodological advantage of the experimental design.

claim: A high-precision dataset was obtained that allowed quantification of even small changes in protein synthesis and degradation with statistical significance.
source: Therefore, we obtained a high-precision dataset that allowed us to quantify even small changes in protein synthesis and degradation with statistical significance; small changes are often missed with label-free or label-free-like (separate evaluation of isotopic channels without internal normalization) experimental designs.
evidence: This describes a methodological advantage of the experimental design.

claim: Small changes in protein synthesis and/or degradation (detected in the whole-cell lysate) might be biologically relevant as they could have a strong local impact either in different neuron types or at specific sub-cellular locations.
source: We believe that small changes in protein synthesis and/or degradation (detected in the whole-cell lysate) might be biologically relevant as they could have a strong local impact either in different neuron types or at specific sub-cellular locations.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the biological significance of small changes detected in the data.

claim: Many of the regulated proteins were previously implicated in synaptic plasticity.
source: In support of our data, many of these regulated proteins were previously implicated in synaptic plasticity.
evidence: This is a statement validating the findings by comparison to prior knowledge.

claim: The study discovered regulation of proteins that were not yet implicated in homeostatic scaling or synaptic plasticity, which are promising candidates for future studies.
source: In addition, we discovered regulation of proteins that were not yet implicated in homeostatic scaling or synaptic plasticity, which are promising candidates for future studies.
evidence: This is a statement about novel findings from the study.

claim: Long-lasting changes in synaptic strength require de-novo protein synthesis as well as the degradation of existing proteins.
source: Long-lasting changes in synaptic strength, which are a basis for learning and memory formation, require de-novo protein synthesis as well as the degradation of existing proteins (Cajigas et al., 2010; Hegde, 2017; Jarome and Helmstetter, 2013; Tai and Schuman, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Injections of the protein synthesis inhibitor puromycin into rodent brains during specific time windows after training blocked long-term memory formation.
source: For example, injections of the protein synthesis inhibitor puromycin (Flexner et al., 1963) or of the proteasome inhibitor lactacystin (Lopez-Salon et al., 2001) into rodent brains during specific time windows after training blocked long-term memory formation.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Injections of the proteasome inhibitor lactacystin into rodent brains during specific time windows after training blocked long-term memory formation.
source: For example, injections of the protein synthesis inhibitor puromycin (Flexner et al., 1963) or of the proteasome inhibitor lactacystin (Lopez-Salon et al., 2001) into rodent brains during specific time windows after training blocked long-term memory formation.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Several forms of synaptic plasticity studied in vitro, including homeostatic scaling, require protein synthesis and degradation.
source: Also, several forms of synaptic plasticity studied in vitro, including homeostatic scaling, require protein synthesis and degradation (Ehlers, 2003; Kang and Schuman, 1996; Rosenberg et al., 2014; Schanzenbächer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Homeostatic scaling is a compensatory mechanism that enables neurons to adjust the synaptic strength in response to persistent changes in the network activity.
source: Homeostatic scaling is a compensatory mechanism that enables neurons to adjust the synaptic strength in response to persistent changes in the network activity.
evidence: This is a definition of homeostatic scaling based on established knowledge.

claim: Homeostatic down-scaling reduces synaptic strength, at least in part by AMPA receptor (AMPAR) internalization.
source: While homeostatic down-scaling reduces synaptic strength, at least in part by AMPA (α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid) receptor (AMPAR) internalization, the opposite is true for homeostatic up-scaling, which increases synaptic strength by increased AMPAR surface expression (Turrigiano, 2012; Turrigiano, 2008; Turrigiano et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Homeostatic up-scaling increases synaptic strength by increased AMPAR surface expression.
source: While homeostatic down-scaling reduces synaptic strength, at least in part by AMPA (α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid) receptor (AMPAR) internalization, the opposite is true for homeostatic up-scaling, which increases synaptic strength by increased AMPAR surface expression (Turrigiano, 2012; Turrigiano, 2008; Turrigiano et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Homeostatic scaling cannot be evoked in the presence of protein synthesis inhibitors or proteasome inhibitors.
source: However, homeostatic scaling cannot be evoked in the presence of protein synthesis inhibitors or proteasome inhibitors (Ehlers, 2003; Schanzenbächer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Information is stored in the specific combination of proteins that are present in neurons, especially at synapses.
source: These findings suggest that information is stored in the specific combination of proteins that are present in neurons, especially at synapses.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the requirement for protein synthesis and degradation in memory formation.

claim: Although memories can last for a lifetime, most neuronal proteins are continuously turned over and only a small fraction of neuronal proteins have been reported to be extremely long-lived.
source: However, although memories can last for a lifetime, most neuronal proteins are continuously turned over and only a small fraction of neuronal proteins have been reported to be extremely long-lived (Toyama et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: In-vivo studies reported average protein half-lives of 9.0–10.7 days in the mouse brain.
source: In-vivo studies reported average protein half-lives of 9.0–10.7 days in the mouse brain (Fornasiero et al., 2018; Price et al., 2010), whereas protein half-lives determined in culture are comparably shorter (on average 2.3–5.9 days) (Cohen et al., 2013; Dörrbaum et al., 2018; Mathieson et al., 2018) but correlate well with the in vivo data (Fornasiero et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Protein half-lives determined in culture are comparably shorter (on average 2.3–5.9 days) but correlate well with the in vivo data.
source: In-vivo studies reported average protein half-lives of 9.0–10.7 days in the mouse brain (Fornasiero et al., 2018; Price et al., 2010), whereas protein half-lives determined in culture are comparably shorter (on average 2.3–5.9 days) (Cohen et al., 2013; Dörrbaum et al., 2018; Mathieson et al., 2018) but correlate well with the in vivo data (Fornasiero et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Continuous protein turnover is essential to maintain a functional pool of proteins and impaired protein degradation is implicated in various neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Continuous protein turnover is essential to maintain a functional pool of proteins and impaired protein degradation is implicated in various neurodegenerative diseases (Boland et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

source: Previous studies used candidate-based approaches to show the differential expression during synaptic scaling of selected proteins, such as Bdnf (Rutherford et al., 1998) or PSD-95 (Sun and Turrigiano, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: Schanzenbächer et al. used BONCAT-MS to analyze the nascent proteome during homeostatic scaling and reported that hundreds of proteins showed regulated synthesis rates.
source: Schanzenbächer et al. used BONCAT-MS to analyze the nascent proteome during homeostatic scaling and reported that hundreds of proteins showed regulated synthesis rates (Schanzenbächer et al., 2018; Schanzenbächer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited literature.

claim: The contributions of protein synthesis and degradation to changes in protein abundance levels and protein turnover rates during synaptic plasticity have not yet been systematically studied.
source: The contributions of protein synthesis and degradation to changes in protein abundance levels and protein turnover rates during synaptic plasticity have not yet been systematically studied.
evidence: This is a statement identifying a gap in the literature that the current study addresses.

claim: The data represent the most comprehensive analysis of proteome dynamics associated with homeostatic scaling to date.
source: Our data represent the most comprehensive analysis of proteome dynamics associated with homeostatic scaling to date, revealing that large fractions of the neuronal proteome, especially synaptic proteins, are affected by this scaling.
evidence: This is a claim about the significance and comprehensiveness of the current study.

claim: A large fraction of the neuronal proteome shows changes in protein synthesis and/or degradation during homeostatic up- and down-scaling.
source: Our data demonstrate that a large fraction of the neuronal proteome shows changes in protein synthesis and/or degradation during homeostatic up- and down-scaling.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the Abstract.
